Question: Describe your cloud-native architecture. How does the platform handle elastic scaling and serverless execution for varying agent workloads?
Response: Our architecture is cloud-native on Azure with three cooperating execution layers under a Fleet Manager governance tier. (a) Azure Durable Functions (GA) — the long-running durable envelope around each workflow: one instance per workflow, event-driven phase routing, HITL waits at zero compute, timer escalation, parallel coordination, checkpoint/replay and geo-replicated state. (b) Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) workflows v1.0 — the per-phase graph of typed executors (plain-function, agent, validator) with Pregel BSP execution, conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in and native pause/resume. DF↔MAF integration uses Microsoft's productised MAF Durable Task extension for Azure Functions (the "Durable Agent Orchestration" pattern, Feb 2026). (c) GHCP SDK sessions — invoked only from MAF agent executor nodes where LLM reasoning is genuinely required; ephemeral, load skills + MCP tools, emit OTEL, exit. Above these, Fleet Manager agents (always-on GHCP SDK Hosted Agents on Azure AI Foundry) govern fleet health and compose exception queues. Scaling is handled at each layer independently: DF auto-scales with consumption plan; MAF graphs scale within DF activities; GHCP SDK sessions are ephemeral. APIM AI Gateway sits centrally governing all model calls, MCP tool invocations and agent interactions (load balancing, failover, token limits, cost tracking). APIM operates in Private Endpoint mode as the sole public edge; all backends (Cosmos DB, Key Vault, AI Search, Log Analytics, Event Grid, Foundry model endpoints) sit behind Private Endpoints; Azure Functions runs with VNet integration; Foundry Hosted Agents are deployed in dedicated subnets with no public IPs; outbound traffic to SaaS (Workday, LinkedIn, Greenhouse, HeyGen, D365, Okta, Maconomy) is restricted to an FQDN allow-list enforced by Azure Firewall Premium. Idle workflows (waiting for approval) consume zero compute; active phases scale elastically.
Key Technologies: Azure AI Foundry Hosted Agents, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0, MAF Durable Task extension, Azure Durable Functions, APIM AI Gateway, GHCP SDK
POC Demo: Show 30-50 concurrent invoice workflows in POC1 with mixed states (active processing, waiting for approval, completed) demonstrating zero-compute waits and elastic phase execution.

Question: What are your high availability and disaster recovery capabilities? Provide multi-region DR details including RTO/RPO SLAs.
Response: HA/DR is provided by Azure's infrastructure across all three execution layers. Durable Functions uses Azure Storage for checkpoint persistence with geo-redundant storage (GRS) replication across paired regions. MAF workflow graph checkpoints are preserved across DF replay via the MAF Durable Task extension, so per-phase graph state survives region failover. Workflow state in Cosmos DB supports multi-region writes with automatic failover. Foundry Hosted Agents deploy across availability zones within a region. APIM AI Gateway supports multi-region deployment with Azure Traffic Manager for automatic failover. RTO target: <5 minutes via automated failover at the Azure platform level. RPO target: near-zero for workflow state (Cosmos DB continuous backup with point-in-time restore) and minimal step loss for in-flight GHCP SDK sessions inside agent executors (checkpointing at MAF executor + DF phase boundaries means at most the current executor replays). Audit logs in Azure Log Analytics support geo-redundant archive with 7-12 year retention (immutability via Azure Storage export with immutability policies). Region-pinned per jurisdiction — EU workflows never resolve US-region endpoints; residency is an enforced boundary via APIOps CI gate which rejects PRs that register cross-region backends. All components are backed by Azure's financially-backed SLAs.
Key Technologies: Azure Cosmos DB (multi-region), Azure Storage GRS, Azure Traffic Manager, Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) Durable Task extension, Azure Log Analytics
POC Demo: Demonstrate mid-workflow platform restart in POC1: kill the hosting environment, show workflow resumes from last checkpoint with no data loss.

Question: Describe your licensing model. How does pricing scale with agent count, model usage, and transaction volume?
Response: Consumption-based Azure pricing across all components. Foundry Hosted Agents: pay-per-agent-run plus storage and compute. Model inference: pay-per-token via Azure OpenAI / Foundry model catalog (tiered model selection means cost optimisation is architectural — cheap models for keyword filtering and triage, frontier models only for high-value reasoning). Durable Functions: consumption plan pricing (pay only for active execution, zero cost during HITL waits). APIM AI Gateway: standard APIM pricing with AI gateway features. Cosmos DB: request unit pricing with reserved capacity discounts. No per-agent-seat licensing — scaling is linear with usage. GHCP SDK is open-source (MIT licence). Volume discounts aligned with WPP's existing Enterprise Agreement. Full cost transparency: per-workflow, per-phase, per-model-call cost attribution visible in Control Plane via OTEL telemetry and APIM metrics.
